summary: Preserved candidate PR 2519's valid fragmented end-marker fix and corrected the independently reproduced one-character marker fragmentation, singular K2-Thinking section markers, unbounded unclosed sections, and missing explicit reset path.

tests.command: inline deterministic parser harness against detached candidate a8cd992b18403cd79c7b1defed0d6862f91f813c using the prepared Python interpreter
tests.what_was_measured: Candidate produced zero calls for one-character wire fragmentation, leaked singular section markers, buffered 600067 characters for an unclosed section with no normal text, and exposed no reset method. Raw output: reports/j-e9fe954d7d7e/candidate-failing-before.txt
Complete dedicated detector suite: 67 passed plus 7 subtests, including all four review counterexamples and the candidate's split-end regression.

gpu_execution.evidence: The corrected behavior is deterministic CPU-only string parsing; no unrelated GPU smoke was used as evidence.

remaining_limitations: No Kimi-K2/K2.5 weights were available, so model semantic accuracy, actual token generation, HTTP client behavior, and distributed execution remain unverified.
The streaming parser API has no end-of-stream signal; a trailing literal '<' is held until a subsequent increment disambiguates it, then emitted unchanged if it is not a marker.
Callers that intentionally reuse a detector across requests must invoke the new reset() method because parse_streaming_increment has no request-boundary argument.
